title: Anticipatory Failure Signature Library and Operator Playbook
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook documents a curated library of "anticipatory" failure signatures (pre-failure signals that reliably precede degradation) and prescribes operator and automated platform responses for LLM inference services. The goal is to detect and act on high-confidence precursors to service-level incidents (latency spikes, token cost overruns, degraded output quality) so we can prevent customer-visible SLO violations.

Scope

- Applies to components in the inference path owned by eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime: request-router, batcher, kv-prefix-cache, model-worker-pool, regional-allocator, edge-proxy.
- Focuses on production-hosted and Dedicated pools. Private deployments should adopt the same patterns but validate thresholds against their metrics.

Definitions

- Failure signature: a concise, observable combination of telemetry signals that historically precedes an incident with >= 75% precision in historical sims.
- Prefailure window: the typical time between signature detection and full degradation (minutes). Used to choose mitigation steps.
- Operator action: human-facing steps in the runbook.
- Automated action: system-initiated response (traffic drain, model-swap, tenant soft-throttle).

How to use this document

1) Operators and platform engineers should review the signature list and corresponding dashboards.
2) Add/modify signatures only after A/B testing in the synthetic-lab and gating in the telemetry-sanity pipeline.
3) For any signature change, update the "anticipatory-signature-registry" (internal dataset) and notify on #platform-prefailure.

Failure Signatures (catalog)

Table: signature | primary signals | confidence | prefailure window | typical root causes | suggested immediate action

1) Batch head-of-line pressure
- primary signals: > 90th-percentile queueing_time_ms for small requests (QPS-normalized) and sudden increase in batch head size variance
- confidence: 0.82
- prefailure window: 2–6 minutes
- typical root causes: hotspot tenant, degraded model-worker CPU scheduling, kernel interference on GPU host
- suggested immediate action: automatically enable per-tenant soft-throttle (10% drop) + alert to operators; pre-warm an alternate worker pool and prepare model-swap (automated).

2) KV-prefix-cache inconsistency spike
- primary signals: partial_cache_hit_rate drop > 12% coupled with a rise in kv-miss-latency P95 by > 5x
- confidence: 0.78
- prefailure window: 1–4 minutes
- typical root causes: cache shard rebalancing, metadata GC bug, cache-corruption event
- suggested immediate action: trigger a cache-cohort read-only fallback (serve from origin), run cache-repair job in the background, notify cache-owners.

3) Model warmset thrash
- primary signals: worker_restarts_per_min > 3 for same model-version + slow_kv_restore_ms > 2000
- confidence: 0.74
- prefailure window: 3–8 minutes
- typical root causes: bad quantization kernels, recent kernel switching rollout, memory fragmentation on GPU nodes
- suggested immediate action: rollback JIT-kernel flag for affected pool, quiesce new rollouts, auto-scale warm replicas.

4) Edge proxy TLS handshake surge with connection churn
- primary signals: tls_handshake_errors_rate P95 > 1% and active_conn_open_rate spike with short-living connections
- confidence: 0.80
- prefailure window: 1–3 minutes
- typical root causes: client library regression, bot traffic surge, healthcheck misconfiguration
- suggested immediate action: enable stricter client-rate-limit layer and route suspicious IPs to regional-scrubbing; open incident channel to partner integrations.

5) Token-cost anomaly during steady traffic
- primary signals: per-request_token_cost increase > 40% vs baseline for 5m and model_entropy_metric drift > 0.12
- confidence: 0.76
- prefailure window: 5–15 minutes
- typical root causes: prompt injection, model hallucination loop, model-variant misrouting
- suggested immediate action: auto-fallback to cost-safe model-variant, snapshot suspect requests for evaluation, throttle heavy tenants if needed.

Detection signals and thresholds (examples)

- All thresholds are initial recommendations. Validate with synthetic-lab and adjust per-region.
- Queueing time spike: queueing_time_ms p95 > baseline_p95 * 2.5 for 3 consecutive 10s windows.
- Cache hit drop: moving average drop of > 10% over 1 minute AND p95 kv-miss-latency > 150ms.
- Worker restarts: same-model restarts > 2 in 5 minutes on a single host.
- TLS churn: tls_handshake_errors_rate > 0.01 AND connection churn rate > 3x baseline.
- Token cost: per_request_token_cost 5m mean > baseline * 1.4 AND model_entropy drift > 0.1.

Automated responses (ordered by risk)

- Low-risk automated actions (no human approval): metric-gated soft throttles, route to warm spare pool, serve fallback model-variant, fetch-memory-prefetch for hot prefixes.
- Medium-risk automated actions (operator-notify + automated): auto-drain single host, pause ongoing kernel switch rollout in a pool, start cache-repair job.
- High-risk automated actions (operator approval required): cross-region failover, tenant eviction, forced model rollback.

Operator runbook (first-responder checklist)

1) Alert triage
- When an anticipatory signature alert fires, the primary oncall (platform) should:
  a) Confirm alert fidelity via the synthetic-signal-replay dashboard and check the prefailure confidence score.
  b) Check correlated signals: CPU/GPU thermal, host kernel messages (/var/log/kern.log), recent rollout tags.

2) Containment
- If signature == batch head-of-line pressure: enable per-tenant soft-throttle for affected tenant ids, increase batch-shed threshold to reduce head growth.
- If signature == kv-prefix-cache inconsistency: switch serving for affected prefixes to read-through mode and mark cache-cohort as degraded.

3) Mitigation
- Follow the automated mitigation in the signature mapping. If automated action succeeded, monitor for 10 minutes. If not resolved, escalate to owner_team oncall.

4) Recovery
- If a model-swap or rollback is performed, perform smoke tests (generate 10 synthetic prompts across the tenant spectrum), check latency SLI and correctness evals for the prompt cohort.

5) Post-action recording
- Record actions taken in the incident ticket (PagerDuty/Incident Jira). Tag with signature id and include links to dashboards and the synthetic cohort snapshot.

Dashboard templates and alerting rules

- Each signature must have a dedicated Grafana panel set: signal overview, top correlated hosts/tenants, recent rollout tags, and synthetic-replay trace. Use panel naming convention: "prefailure.<signature_id>.<view>".
- Example Prometheus-style alert (YAML):
  - alert: Prefailure_Batch_HEAD_Blocking
    expr: (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_queueing_time_bucket[1m])) by (le)) > (baseline_p95 * 2.5)) and (increase(batch_head_variance[2m]) > 0.25)
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: warning
      category: prefailure
    annotations:
      runbook: https://confluence.internal/eng-platform/systems-and-services/anticipatory-failure-signature-library-and-operator-playbook-2026#Operator-runbook

SLI/SLO mapping and customer impact

- Map signatures to SLOs (examples):
  - Batch head-of-line pressure -> Latency SLO: 99th token latency < 800ms. If signature fires, customer risk = elevated tail latency leading to degraded UX.
  - KV-prefix-cache inconsistency -> Availability SLO: 99.9% successful request rate. If signature fires, customer risk = transient error elevation and increased cost.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owners: eng-platform (operators), eng-serving-runtime (runtime specialists).
- Escalation path: primary oncall -> runtime lead -> eng-platform manager -> infra SRE escalation.
- Contact channel: #platform-prefailure (PagerDuty linked). For P1-level escalation use PD channel 'platform-p1'.

Runbook run-through (operational rehearsal)

- Quarterly game-day: run an injected signature simulation in the synthetic-lab and perform full operator runbook. Document time-to-contain, time-to-recover, and automation effectiveness.
- Playbook owner should run a micro-retrospective within 72 hours and fill the template below.

Post-incident retrospective template

1) Incident summary: signature id, prefailure window, impacted pools/tenants.
2) Timeline: detection -> containment -> mitigation -> recovery.
3) Actions taken: automated and operator steps, with timestamps.
4) Root cause hypothesis and evidence.
5) Follow-ups: telemetry fixes, automation tuning, dashboard adjustments, rollout guard amendments.

Safety and false-positive controls

- To avoid alert noise: require composite conditions (two or more signals) for medium/high confidence signatures.
- Use a staged alert path: metric-only -> email/Slack -> oncall page based on persistence and amplification.
- Always include the confidence score and recent synthetic-lab replay result in the alert annotation.

Integration with roadmap and instrumentation backlog

- Short-term (Q1–Q2 2026): instrument missing host-side kernel metrics, implement confidence scoring in alertmanager, add synthetic-replay URLs into alerts.
- Medium-term (H2 2026): enable auto-scaling playbooks tied to signature detection and operator-simulated canary rollouts.
- Long-term (2027): machine-learning based signature discovery pipeline integrated with eval-harness and live A/B testing.

Appendix: synthetic-lab validation checklist

- Verify signal precision >= 0.70 on replayed incidents.
- Run signature through 1000 synthetic tenants with mixed traffic profiles.
- Document false-positive rate and expected operator cost per month.

Ownership and maintenance

- Playbook owner: Sofia Patel (eng-platform).
- Maintenance cadence: sign-off review every 90 days or after any P1 that used a prefailure action.

Contact and feedback

- For questions or to propose new signatures, open a PR against the telemetry-signature-registry and ping @sofia on #platform-prefailure.
